title: product-prd-unified-inference-overview-roadmap-pricing-2025-11-01
author: Maya Chen
summary: This document bundles the product overview, PRD requirements, design specification, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product family. It is intended for engineering, product, go-to-market, and support teams responsible for shipping and operating inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
overview:
Purpose
- Provide a single source-of-truth for Unified Inference: goals, scope, and success metrics.
- Align engineering work and GTM motion for the next 6 quarters.

Problem statement
- Customers need a unified runtime and API that gives predictable latency/cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Fragmented configs and unclear price/performance tradeoffs slow adoption for production use.

Product goals (measurable)
1) Reduce average per-token cost for typical chat workloads by 25% vs. baseline (2025 Q4).
2) Achieve 99.95% service availability for hosted API and meet p95 latency SLOs for common endpoints.
3) Provide a single API and rollout experience across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with consistent observability.

Target personas
- ML engineers embedding LLM features into products.
- Platform teams standardizing inference across business units.
- Enterprise security/compliance teams evaluating Private deployments.

Key surface areas
- Redwood API (text, chat, embeddings, reranking)
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools, autoscaling)
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)
- Redwood Console (observability & rollouts)
- Redwood Optimize (cost/perf toolkit)
requirements:
Functional requirements
1) Single, backwards-compatible HTTP/JSON API for text generation and chat.
   - Endpoint: POST /v1/unified/generate
   - Supports streaming responses and function/tool calling.
   - Must accept model pinning metadata (model_id, model_variant, quantization_profile).
2) Smart routing policy engine.
   - Route by policy attributes: latency_target, cost_preference, customer_tier, region.
   - Fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained.
3) Autoscaling + reserved capacity for Dedicated.
   - Policy language to express min_capacity, max_capacity, burst_ratio, cooldown_seconds.
4) Quality monitoring and regression detection.
   - Per-customer eval sets, baseline metrics, and alerting on regression thresholds.

Non-functional requirements
- Availability: 99.95% for hosted API (monthly).
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 75ms, p95 < 250ms for common text-gen (seq_len=256) on hosted in-region.
- Cost telemetry: token-level cost attribution exposed via Console and billing exports.
- Security: support KMS integrations, RBAC, and audit logging for Private installs.

Acceptance criteria (sample table described)
- Table: columns = [requirement_id, description, owner, priority, acceptance_criteria]
- Example row: [REQ-API-01, Backwards-compatible generation endpoint, eng-dex, P0, unit+integration tests + e2e smoke + SDK samples]

Owners

- API & SDK: Eng DevEx (owner: Arjun Patel).
- Routing & runtime: Eng Serving Runtime (owner: Sofia Martinez).
- Dedicated infra & billing: Eng SRE (owner: Liam O'Neill).
design_spec:
High-level architecture
- Components:
  1) redwood-unified-api: HTTP façade that handles auth, quota, basic validation and transforms requests into routing tokens.
  2) routing-service: policy evaluation, region/capacity selection, model-variant fallback logic.
  3) serving-runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine (batching, KV cache, quantization execution paths).
  4) optimize-suggester: offline/online analysis engine that recommends batching/quantization profiles.
  5) console-backend: observability dashboarding and rollout controls.

Sequence flow (request)
1) Client -> redwood-unified-api (auth + quota).
2) API -> routing-service (policy evaluation).
3) routing-service selects target pool and model variant -> serving-runtime.
4) serving-runtime streams tokens back to unified-api -> client.

API contract (example JSON)
{
  "model_id": "redwood/gptx-8b",
  "model_variant": "gptx-8b-fp16-q4_0",
  "prompt": "<user prompt>",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "stream": true,
  "routing": { "latency_target_ms": 250, "cost_preference": "balanced" }
}

Configuration & deployment matrix (described table)
- Table columns: [component, default_config, production_scale_example, owner]
- Example rows described: routing-service default concurrency=200, production_cluster=3x N, owner=eng-serving-runtime; serving-runtime default batch_window_ms=10, kv_cache_size=4GB per GPU.

Performance tuning knobs (prioritized)
- batch_window_ms, max_batch_tokens, kv_cache_policy, quantization_profile, kernel_selection_hint.

Observability contract
- Traces: request_id, route_decision, model_variant, request_latency_ms, tokens_generated, cost_estimate_micro_usd.
- Metrics: per-route qps, per-model p50/p95 latency, cache_hit_ratio, average_batch_size.
- Logs: structured JSON with correlation_id and deploy_tag.

Security & compliance notes
- Private installs must support HSM-backed KMS and keep all inference logs behind customer VPC by default.
- Audit events emitted for model version changes, rollout actions, and key management operations.
roadmap_and_themes:
Roadmap (6-quarter view)
Q4 2025 (launched)
- GA unified API, streaming and function calling.
- Basic routing policies and Hosted GA.
Q1 2026
- Redwood Optimize v2: model & quantization recommendations.
- Dedicated reserved capacity beta with autoscale policies.
Q2 2026
- Private VPC beta and on-prem packaging for regulated customers.
- Console rollout features: canary, A/B test UI, automatic fallback.
Q3 2026
- SLO-driven routing and adaptive batching.
- Price-tiering controls in Console and per-customer billing exports.
Q4 2026
- Advanced quality guardrails: per-customer evals + auto rollback on regressions.
Q1 2027
- Multi-region active-active routing and cross-region failover.

Themes
- Production economics: reduce cost per useful token with batching, caching and quantization.
- Predictability: reserved capacity, robust fallbacks, and deterministic rollouts.
- Developer experience: simple API, clear SDKs, and transparent perf benchmarks.

Milestones & success metrics
- GA Hosted unified API adoption: 200 customers onboarded and >$1M ARR from usage within first 6 months.
- Dedicated: 20 customers on reserved capacity with committed contracts > $X/month.
- Latency & reliability: maintain p95 latency under 250ms and availability >= 99.95%.
pricing_and_packaging:
Pricing principles
- Usage-based simplicity for Hosted: per-token rates for generation and per-embedding unit.
- Predictable economics for Dedicated: monthly committed spend with discounts and burst capacity add-on.
- Enterprise Private: platform licensing + deployment + premium support.

Sample pricing tiers (example numbers)
- Hosted (Pay-as-you-go):
  * Generation: $0.006 per 1K input tokens, $0.012 per 1K output tokens for gptx-8b class.
  * Embeddings: $0.0025 per 1K vector units.
  * Streaming surcharge: +10% for realtime streaming endpoints.
- Dedicated (example commit):
  * 4x A100-equivalent reserved pool: $30,000/month commit -> includes baseline throughput 50 RPS for seq_len=256, overage billed at $X per token.
  * Autoscale burst add-on: 20% of commit for short bursts at additional 25% premium.
- Private license: $200K/year platform fee + deployment professional services and support tiers.

Packaging notes
- Free tier: dev sandbox with 40k tokens/month for quick experimentation.
- Enterprise tier includes audit logging, extended retention, and on-call support.

Pricing examples (worked)
- Customer A (chat bot): 2M input tokens + 4M output tokens / month using gptx-8b -> cost = (2M/1K)*$0.006 + (4M/1K)*$0.012 = $12 + $48 = $60/month (hosted).

Billing & metering contract points
- Tokenization rules and normalization are applied at ingestion.
- Billing export: daily CSV/BigQuery export with per-request cost attribution.
- Discounts & committed usage are managed via billing account with usage thresholds and audit trail.
release_notes:
Release: Unified Inference v1.3 (2026-03-04)
Release summary
- Added: Dedicated reserved capacity (beta) with autoscaling policies.
- Added: Advanced routing policy attributes (latency_target_ms, cost_preference).
- Improved: Serving runtime kernel selection improved p95 latency by ~18% on seq_len=256.
- Fixed: KV cache leak under high-concurrency workloads.

Breaking changes
- None for v1.3; all API additions are backwards compatible.

Migration notes
- Customers using legacy /v1/generate should be able to call /v1/unified/generate with identical body; prefer model pinning fields for future-proofing.

Rollout plan
1) Internal canary (day 0): route 2% of internal traffic, monitor key metrics for 6 hours.
2) Gradual customer canary (day 1-3): route 5% -> 20% -> 50% for opt-in customers.
3) Global rollout (day 4-7): increment to 100% with staged region-by-region enablement.

Monitoring & rollback criteria
- Abort and rollback if any of the following sustained for 10 minutes:
  * Error rate > 1% (baseline 0.1%).
  * p95 latency regresses by > 30% vs baseline.
  * Increased unit cost estimate > 25% for top 5 customers.

Owners & contacts

rollout_and_operational_playbook:
Canary & rollback runbook
Pre-checks (pre-release)
- Verify e2e smoke tests pass in staging against GA models.
- Confirm capacity availability: dedicated pools healthy and autoscalers green.
- Notify GTM and support teams via #releases channel with change details and postmortem owners.

Canary steps
1) Internal canary: enable new routing policy rules for internal org only. Monitor metrics dashboard.
2) Customer canary: opt-in flag in Console that allows customers to join canary cohorts. Start with 10 customers representing low, medium, high QPS.
3) Incremental ramp: double traffic to new rollout every 6 hours until reaching 100% or rollback triggers fire.

Rollback procedure
1) Route traffic back to previous stable release via routing-service control plane.
2) If rollback fails, disable new model variants and scale up older pools.
3) Open incident in PagerDuty, assign triage lead, and notify stakeholders.

Post-release checks (24-72 hours)
- Verify no customer regressions reported via support.
- Confirm no long-tail memory/GPU leaks in serving runtime.
- Run regression evals against holdout prompt sets and compare to baseline metrics.

SLOs & alert thresholds
- Availability SLO: 99.95% (monthly), alert at 99.9%.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 75ms (alert if p50 > 150ms).
- Error budget burn alert: 25% of monthly error budget consumed -> paging to SRE lead.

Runbook owners
- Runbook author: Liam O'Neill (eng-sre).
- On-call escalation: follow eng-sre oncall rotation.
- Postmortem owner: product (Maya Chen) for customer-impacting incidents.
